County analysis data from the 2020–2024 ACS five-year Data Profiles

acs2020_2024_counties.Rd

The 3,107-county analysis table used in Nonconvex Geographically Weighted Regression for Local Variable Selection. The 91 columns retain the study's estimates, 90 percent margins of error, controlled-MOE flags, identifiers, projected coordinates and saved spatial folds.

Usage

data(acs2020_2024_counties)

Format

A data frame with 3,107 rows and 91 columns:

fips

Five-character county FIPS identifier; leading zeros retained. .

county_name

Census county or county-equivalent name. .

state_fips

Two-character state FIPS identifier. .

state_abbreviation

Two-letter postal abbreviation. .

state_name

State name. .

county_fips

Three-character within-state county FIPS identifier. .

easting_m

Easting of a point on the county surface after projection to NAD83 / Conus Albers (EPSG:5070); not longitude or latitude. metres.

northing_m

Northing of a point on the county surface after projection to NAD83 / Conus Albers (EPSG:5070); not longitude or latitude. metres.

spatial_fold

Saved spatial fold from k-means on standardized projected coordinates; seed 20260907, nstart 100. Fold labels must be reused for the paper analysis. 1 to 5.

median_household_income_2024

Original county median household income estimate, before the natural logarithm. 2024 inflation-adjusted US dollars.

Details

This is a single cross-sectional table with one row per county. The 2024 ACS five-year product contains Census Bureau period estimates based on survey data collected during 2020–2024. The analysis uses these published estimates directly: separate annual observations are neither stacked nor arithmetically averaged. The 2024 suffix in the retained income column names identifies the ACS product and the inflation-adjustment year, not a single-year observation. The legacy dataset name acs2024_counties remains available for compatibility.

The domain is the contiguous 48 states and the District of Columbia. Of 3,109 eligible geographic records, De Baca County, New Mexico (35011), lacks a median household income estimate, and Loving County, Texas (48301), lacks a mean commute estimate. These two records were excluded under the study's complete-case estimate policy. Alaska, Hawaii and territories are outside the domain. No estimate is imputed, winsorized or standardized in this data object.

The response is the natural logarithm of income in 2024 inflation-adjusted dollars. Predictors remain in their original units. Percentage estimates use the populations stated in the Census labels; they do not all share the same denominator. County associations do not identify individual-level or causal effects.

A Census controlled-estimate MOE sentinel (-555555555) is stored as zero and marked by a logical companion column. Other unavailable MOEs were treated as missing without automatic sample exclusion; this released table contains no missing values. In particular, log_median_household_income_2024__moe90 retains the original dollar-scale income MOE. It is not an MOE on the log scale and must not be used as one.

The spatial folds use projected representative points, seed 20260907 and 100 k-means starts. Coordinates are metres in EPSG:5070 and are not geographic longitude/latitude. Polygon geometry and the common diagnostic graph are provided in the separate reproduction bundle, not in this data frame.

The machine-readable 91-column dictionary and provenance record are installed under system.file("extdata", package = "gwrs"). Preparation code and the public source snapshot are included in the repository's reproduction bundle.

Source

U.S. Census Bureau, 2020–2024 American Community Survey five-year Data Profiles, downloaded 7 September 2026: https://api.census.gov/data/2024/acs/acs5/profile.html. County and state cartographic boundaries: https://www.census.gov/geographies/mapping-files/time-series/geo/cartographic-boundary.html.

References

U.S. Census Bureau. 2020–2024 American Community Survey five-year Data Profiles.

Yuzbasi, B. (2026). Nonconvex Geographically Weighted Regression for Local Variable Selection. Manuscript.

For work using this prepared dataset, please acknowledge the Census source, the accompanying paper and gwrs. Use citation("gwrs") for package citation information.

Examples

data(acs2020_2024_counties)
dim(acs2020_2024_counties)
head(acs2020_2024_counties[, c("fips", "county_name",
                         "median_household_income_2024", "spatial_fold")])
dictionary <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "acs2020_2024_counties_dictionary.csv",
                                   package = "gwrs"))
head(dictionary)
